seeds.prompt: Define one canonical field envelope for {project, run, seam, package, node, attempt, lane, promotion, review, resolution_thread} so schemas stop drifting independently.
seeds.why_it_matters: Schema drift is currently occurring across independently evolving docs.

seeds.prompt: Decide whether tier terms become pure derived UI aliases or are fully deprecated in orchestration/runtime contracts.
seeds.why_it_matters: Contract language is split between old tier semantics and new runtime model.

seeds.prompt: Decide how package overseer and seam overseer divide authority across scheduling, review, promotion, remediation, and graph patch requests.
seeds.why_it_matters: Authority boundaries are unresolved across major control surfaces.

seeds.prompt: Formalize requested vs effective execution identity, including account fallback/switching, before provider/chat/SCM docs extend the wrong model.
seeds.why_it_matters: Identity semantics are expanding without a stable canonical definition.

seeds.prompt: Define package-based lane-pool worktree policy end-to-end, including contamination, safe-point, restore, and visibility rules shared by Orchestrator and Source Control.
seeds.why_it_matters: Policy is split and risks divergent orchestration vs SCM behavior.

seeds.prompt: Unify blocked/recovery action families so UI, runtime, and chat-thread resolution all point to the same canonical actions.
seeds.why_it_matters: Action semantics are currently fragmented across surfaces.

findings: Source Control is primary for worktree inventory and user actions.
Orchestrator consumes worktree identity/ownership/blocked-state/lineage for run and recovery views.
Settings surfaces are config/diagnostics, not primary active-worktree management.
Docs remain runtime-worktree-centric and tier-bound, colliding with package-based lane-pool direction.
Storage direction is close: receipts and project state already carry key SCM/worktree linkage fields.
Cleanup semantics exist but are not normalized between lane lifecycle and workspace-file cleanup actions.

orchestrator: Own package lane-pool operational truth for active runs.
Explain blocked, weakly integrated, and cleanup-eligible state.
source_control: Own repo/worktree execution and inspection operations.
Provide explicit disabled reasons for destructive actions.

model_shift: Move user-visible stack toward Feature Seam > Work Package > Lane > Worktree.
Make Lane the primary operational object in Orchestrator.
Keep Worktree as concrete filesystem/Git backing of lane instances.
Preserve lane historical identity after worktree cleanup/archive/removal.
Allow Source Control worktree listings while exposing lane/package lifecycle ownership.

interpretation: historical is record truth and can coexist with archived or removed.
archived keeps metadata/lineage visible while execution is inactive.
removed indicates live worktree directory is gone.
cleanup_eligible is a queued policy state, not already removed.
suspect/restoring should surface first in Orchestrator, second in Source Control.

findings: Requested/effective execution identity is stronger on effective side than requested side.
No canonical requested concrete-account anchor exists for explicit account pinning.
Identity chain is split across effective_account_id, effective_provider_identity, and provider_account_id without governing rule.
Bridged-provider contracts omit requested/effective auth-account fields present in canonical runtime contract.
Identity docs remain tier-bound and not rewritten for node/package/seam/lane ownership.
Permissions model lacks execution-entity/lane/account-bounded resolution in parallel-actor runs.

docs.risk: Missing durable switch-history storage and scheduler/usage identity alignment.
Stops short of requested concrete-account identity; still carries tier-era ownership framing.
Insufficient for canonical account identity, switch-reason disclosure, and actor routing.
Contradictory canonical field naming; no overseer persona model/account disclosure rule.
Cannot express lane/package/account-bounded permission resolution and approval scope.

items: Personas runtime section still uses requested_persona_id/effective_persona_id despite canonical prohibition in Contracts_V0.
Requested_account_policy exists without a requested concrete-account companion field.
Bridged providers are effectively exempt from multi-account capability declaration by omission.
Provider OpenCode and stream mapping docs assume account disclosure not supported by current mappings.
Permissions hints exist but no general execution-entity narrowing rule for crew/member/lane/account scopes.

fixes: Add one canonical requested-side concrete-account field while keeping requested_account_policy as routing policy.
Govern provider_account_id as either retired or explicitly provider-native metadata under effective_account_id.
Unify bridged-provider request/persistence envelopes with Contracts_V0 and Prompt_Pipeline auth/account fields.
Replace tier-bound identity/override wording with node/package/seam/lane ownership language.
Add execution-entity, lane, package, and effective-account dimensions to permission resolution and approval carryover/cascade rules.

notes: Missing requested-side account anchor blocks durable requested-vs-effective historical analysis.
provider_account_id inconsistency is now cross-doc across identity, storage, and provider specs.
Bridged runtimes may switch/obscure upstream accounts with no current capture policy.
Overseer persona gap is structural for package- and seam-overseer identity modeling.
Approval scope must not remain implicitly same-session in parallel lane execution.
